title: HB495 (136th Legislature (2025-2026)): Enact the Freedom to Carry Act

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Ohio) (gun-policy Stage 5, Ohio); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Ohio text (As Introduced (00_IN), ; official copy, https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_136/legislation/hb495/00_IN/pdf/ (Open States text id 90137416))
provenance.note: As introduced (136th GA); very large text, key parts quoted. Age for permitless carry: 'Twenty-one' struck, 'Eighteen' added (qualifying adult). 'Restricted firearm' definition struck and replaced by 'exclusive deadly weapon/firearm'. Also amends R.C. 9.68 (preemption widened to all deadly weapons, accessories and attachments), 109.69 (reciprocity), 311.41-.43, 1547.69, 2921.13, 2923.12-.129, 2923.16, 2953.35, 4749.10 and repeals R.C. 1533.04 (suppressors for hunting) in Section 3; sections not read line by line.

operative_text:
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.111(A)(1)(a)): "Qualifying adult" means a person who is all of the following: (a) Eighteen years of age or older.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.111(B)(1)): A person who is a qualifying adult shall not be required to obtain a concealed weapons license in order to carry in this state, under authority of division (B)(2) of this section, a concealed deadly weapon that is not an exclusive deadly weapon.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.111(B)(2)): Regardless of whether the person has been issued a concealed weapons license, subject to the limitations specified in divisions (B)(3) and (C)(2) of this section, a person who is a qualifying adult may carry concealed on the person's person or concealed ready at hand a deadly weapon that is not an exclusive deadly weapon anywhere in this state in which a person who has been issued a concealed weapons license may carry a concealed deadly weapon that is not an exclusive deadly weapon.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.111(A)(2)): "Exclusive deadly weapon" means a deadly weapon that is an exclusive firearm or that is a deadly weapon that any law of this state or the United States prohibits the subject person from acquiring, possessing, having, or carrying.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.111(A)(3)): "Exclusive firearm" means a firearm that is dangerous ordnance or that is a firearm that any law of this state or the United States prohibits the subject person from acquiring, possessing, having, or carrying.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.126(A)): Except as provided in divisions (B) and (C) of this section, a licensee who has been issued a concealed weapons license under section 2923.125 or 2923.1213 of the Revised Code prior to, on, or after the effective date of this amendment may carry a concealed deadly weapon that is not an exclusive deadly weapon anywhere in this state if the license is valid when the licensee is in actual possession of a concealed deadly weapon that is not an exclusive deadly weapon.
